The '''TIE Advanced x1''', also known as '''TIE/x1''' or '''TIE Interceptor prototype''',<ref name="Star Wars Technical Journal of the Imperial Forces">''[[Star Wars Technical Journal of the Imperial Forces]]''</ref> was an [[TIE/Advanced starfighter|advanced prototype]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] touted as a replacement for the standard [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] tested by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and [[X1]] at the battles of [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Yavin]] and [[Battle of Mustafar (Galactic Civil War)|Mustafar]] respectively.
While it never made it into production, many of its best design features were later incorporated into the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]] and [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]]. Further development of the Advanced continued, eventually leading to the [[TIE/ad starfighter|TIE Avenger]] and [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE Defender]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:TIEx1_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|180px|TIE/x1 [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]]]]
The [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] Advanced x1 featured a [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]] [[I-s3a solar ionization reactor/Legends|I-s3a]] [[Solar ionization reactor/Legends|solar ionization reactor]] and paired [[P-s5.6 twin ion engine/Legends|P-s5.6 twin ion engines]] like the original [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]]. However, the x1 had an original spaceframe, with an elongated rear deck and reinforced [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]]-alloy hull. The x1's most important innovation was the use of "bent-wing" solar array wings, like those used on the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]], which had the advantages of increased surface area for more power while also reducing the craft's profile, compared to the TIE/LN starfighter's hexagonal panel wings.

Speed was only slightly improved due to the added mass of the vessel; a good deal of the extra power was bled off to the [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]] generators. While less maneuverable than standard [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] fighters, it was more resilient in battle.

The 9.2 [[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long craft<ref name="BtM" /> had twin heavy [[L-s9.3 laser cannon/Legends|L-s9.3 laser cannons]] in a gimballed, front-mounted position, as well as a [[Cluster missile/Legends|cluster missile]] launcher. In addition to its shields, it had a modest Class 4.0 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] but no [[Life support/Legends|life support]] systems. The target tracking system was also more sophisticated than the already formidable advanced targeting system on standard TIE craft, used to overcome the extremely powerful electronic jamming used by all combat craft to defeat target lock in battle. For best performance, the targeting system of the x1 required frequent adjustment in combat.

Only the most elite [[TIE pilot|Imperial pilots]] flew the TIE Advanced,<ref name="RS II guide" /> and the starfighter was capable of fighting a [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]] to a draw.<ref name="RS III guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>

Seinar Fleet Systems designed many iterations of the TIE Advanced prototype, eventually resulting in an [[TIE Advanced x1 (modified)|improved version]] that possessed solar strakes to the panels in order to increase power distribution.<ref name="SWG">{{SonyCite|url=content.jsp?page=Friday%20Feature:%20Rage%20Of%20The%20Wookiees:%20Ships|text=Friday Feature: Rage Of The Wookiees: Ships}}</ref>

==History==
Wishing to cut all ties with his Jedi past after his [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|fateful duel]], Darth Vader contacted [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar]] with a set of specifications for a new starfighter. Sienar and his team rose to the challenge and, after producing an [[TIE Advanced prototype|early prototype]],<ref name="IH" /> eventually presented Vader with the TIE Advanced x1 model. At least one ended up piloted by [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], when she was still part of the Imperial forces as a member of the [[Black Eight Squadron]].<ref name="The Academy's Finest">{{FantasyFlightGames|url=en/news/2015/5/4/the-academys-finest|text=The Academy's Finest}}</ref> Because of Vader's positive reception to the x1's design, there was hope among the Imperial Naval hierarchy that it would be mass-produced in massive numbers.<ref name="IH" /> In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], several months after the start of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Subject 1138|renegade clone]] of the late [[Galen Marek]] stole Vader's TIE Advanced to [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escape]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and [[Rescue of Rahm Kota|travel]] to [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]].<ref name="TFU2">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref> Vader continued to fly it often afterwards, and even went to some lengths to have it recovered and repaired when damaged during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends#The Trench Run|trench run]] at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin 4]].<ref name="SWE14:TSH">[[Empire 14|''Empire'' 14]]</ref>

[[File:TIENoseLasers-MSW20.jpg|thumb|right|180px|TIE Advanced x1s during an attack on the Wheel]]
Armed with the references of a pleased Darth Vader, Sienar presented his x1 to the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] for mass distribution. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], however, decided not to order the TIE Advanced x1 in large quantities, citing their excessive cost. Privately, some Imperial Navy strategists admitted that the Navy was afraid to purchase a fighter with a hyperdrive, fearing that it would give bureaucrats an excuse to slash orders for new capital starships. Some also feared that hyperdrive-equipped starfighters would facilitate defections. In the end, only a few squadrons were equipped with x1s.

The few ships built were carried aboard [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and other Imperial vessels. TIE Advanced x1s were deployed from [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Zertik Strom/Legends|Strom's]] [[Pursuit-class light cruiser|''Pursuit''-class light cruiser]] to stage an attack on [[The Wheel/Legends|the Wheel]], which the Empire blamed on the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]], excusing the Imperial takeover of the station.<ref name="SW18:TES">[[Star Wars (1977) 18|''Star Wars'' (1977) 18]]</ref> TIE Advanced were also utilized during the events at [[Constancia/Legends|Constancia]], with two being dispatched alongside [[boarding craft 356]] to retrieve a life pod believed to contain a badly injured Luke Skywalker and [[Gamine]] (although in actuality it contained [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Sharlee]] in battle armor.<ref name="The Constancia Affair">"[[The Constancia Affair]]"</ref> [[Storm Squadron/Legends|Storm Squadron]] used x1s extensively.<ref name="SWPMTCG">[[Star Wars PocketModel TCG|''Star Wars'' PocketModel TCG]]</ref> Several x1 starfighters were also in a fleet gathering observed by Admiral [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]] and Captain [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]] at some point between the former's promotion to Admiral and the latter's promotion to Admiral.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

[[File:TIEAdvancedX1AtEndor-ST.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A TIE Advanced x1 and TIE fighters engaging [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wings]] near the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]]]]The fighter flown by Vader at Yavin was repaired when he reached [[Imperial Relay Outpost V-798]].<ref name="SWE14:TSH" /> Vader had it with him on the ''[[Terror]]'', while overseeing the [[TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter/Legends|TIE Phantom]] project. When the ''Terror'' was destroyed by Rebel operatives, Vader escaped in his fighter.<ref name="SW:RAII:THE">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire]]''</ref> Vader again utilized his TIE Advanced x1 during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. However, his ship was damaged and rendered inoperative by Rebel starfighters piloted by members of [[Renegade Squadron/Legends|Renegade Squadron]]<ref name="SWB:RS">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]''</ref>

It was later stowed aboard the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] and was apparently vaporized when the ship collided with the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] during the Battle of Endor, though at least one TIE Advanced x1 was involved in the space battle over the sanctuary moon.<ref name="ST">[[ScreenThemes]]</ref> One of Vader's other TIE Advanced x1 models was discovered by [[Jaden Korr]] in a hangar at Darth Vader's former [[Bast Castle|stronghold]] on [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]].<ref name="SW:JK:JA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> Also, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[X1]] flew such a ship during the [[Battle of Mustafar (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Mustafar]].<ref name="BF:ES">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]''</ref> During the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|liberation of Coruscant]], at least two TIE Advanced x1s, utilized by [[Elite Force]], were tasked with guarding the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]], although they ultimately failed.<ref name="GBCC">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref>

[[File:FlyingBlind-EGF.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Vader's grandchildren flew several TIE Advanced x1]]
By the beginning of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], enough of these ships had been made that some ended up in the hands of private parties such as [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], who used a [[Calrissian Runner|modified TIE Advanced x1]] for entertainment purposes in the asteroid belt at [[Dubrillion/Legends|Dubrillion]]. During the [[Battle of Dubrillion]], [[Darth Caedus|Jacen]], [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina]], and [[Anakin Solo]]&mdash;Vader's grandchildren&mdash;flew three of these fighters against [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yorik-et|coralskippers]].<ref name="VP">''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In Geoffrey Mandel's 1978 blueprints for the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers]], fighters known as "TIE Assault Craft" could be seen as part of the fighter complement. These bent-wing craft might have been TIE Advanced x1s with a different name or possibly a sister craft of the x1.

The size comparison chart found in the [[2011]] reference book ''[[Millennium Falcon Owner's Workshop Manual]]'' suggests a different length for the x1. By using the well-documented sizes of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] and the X-wing as a scale, the resulting size is roughly 7.6 meters.

[[File:TIE_Advanced_x1_starfighter.png|thumb|left|250px|Head-on view of a TIE Advanced x1]]
The x1 is armed with a supply of cluster missiles in its appearance in the game ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''.

The x1 appears to have navigation lights that are like fog lights.

Various x1 starfighters are in the background of an artwork by Tommy Lee Edwards depicting Admiral Ozzel and Captain Piett observing a fleet gathering in the 2012 guidebook ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''. The background itself uses a picture from Ansel Hsiao's personal gallery as a background, originally titled "Strategic Reserve."<ref name="FSG">{{WebCite|url=http://fractalsponge.net/gallery/images/index.html#Strategic%20Reserve.jpg|text=Still Images|author=Ansel Hsiao|archiveurl=https://archive.is/QVVKb}}</ref> According to Ansel Hsiao in an email dated July 18, 2012, when he was creating the artwork, he chose the x1 starfighters to be among the fleet for a few reasons: He hadn't completed any TIEs that utilized a hyperdrive outside of the x1 at the time the artwork was made, and he envisioned the fleet in question as a high-mobility fleet, which required fighters that possessed a functioning hyperdrive. He reasoned that with those needs, units such as the fleet in the image were important enough to have access to limited-production fighters, and that limited-production fighters in a [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning empire would still mean a lot of fighters in a relative sense.<ref name="Email2">{{EmailCite|email=File:FractalSponge_correspondence_part_2.png|creator=Ansel Hsiao|date=2012-07-18}}</ref>

The ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'' game gives the following description of the craft:
<blockquote>''The prototype starfighter used by Darth Vader at the Battle of Yavin and the basis for the frighteningly efficient TIE Interceptor, the TIE Advanced X1 is easily recognizable due to its distinctive bent wings. Unlike all other TIE Fighters, the prototype is equipped with a deflector shield generator and a modest hyperdrive system. The TIE Advanced is armed with fixed twin heavy blaster cannons, but has no life support systems.''</blockquote>
